paragraphs.text: 把 DSH 能读到的 skills 统一扫描、 归并、可视化，解决「skills 太多、不知道哪个命令属于哪个来源」的痛点。
# dsh-skill-catalog

A **DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin** (not a skill): scan every skill your DSH can
load, merge them in

to one browsable catalog, and put it in a sidebar panel —
solving "too many skills, no idea which co

mmand comes from which source".
DSH natively supports `/` invocation, so this plugin only does **cat

aloging and
browsing** — it registers no slash commands of its own.
English | 中文
## Features

- **Single entry point**: a button at the **bottom of the DSH left sidebar**
(next to Settings) open

s a **narrow panel** on the right that sits beside the
conversation instead of covering it.
- **Scan

s exactly what DSH can load**: every direct child of `~/.dsh/skills`
and `~/.agents/skills` becomes

a collection (single-skill directory,
`skills/` skill pack, or loose `.md`). Inclusion rules mirror

DSH's own
source and skill-pack provider loading rules — if DSH won't load it, it is
not listed.
- *

*Refresh**: the ↻ button re-scans `SKILL.md` from disk.
- **Click to insert**: clicking a command ca

rd writes `/command` straight into
the **current conversation input** (via DSH's
`uiSession.current.

value.props.inputActions`, preferring `setDraft(text)`);
falls back to copying to the clipboard when

the composer is unavailable.
- **Right-click for details**: right-click a command card for an info

card
explaining what it does (your custom note takes precedence — see below).
The card flips away fr

om viewport edges; it closes on left-click elsewhere,
Esc, list scroll, the ✕ button, or right-click

ing the same card again.
- **Native tool `dsh_catalog`**: ask in chat "what is /estimate" or "which

skills do I have" and get the three-level catalog (collection › category ›
command) plus the panel a

ddress.
- **Custom categories (saved, persistent)**: paste "category + commands" in
the panel's ⚙ Ca

tegories editor — saved once, effective forever. See
Custom categories.
- **Custom command notes (sa

ved, persistent)**: paste a Markdown table in the
panel's ✎ Notes editor; right-clicking a command t

hen shows your note (the
skill's own description is kept as an "original description" footnote), and

noted commands carry a blue marker and a "noted" badge. See
Custom command notes.
## Scan sources
| Source | Skill location (scan roots) | Parser |
| DeepSeek Harness | `~/.agents/skills` (each child = one collection), `~/.dsh/skills` (the whole ro
ot = one collection) | skill_md |

Three-level structure: **collection › category › command**. Core rules
(mirroring "how DSH reads ski

level structure: **collection › category › command**. Core rules
(mirroring "how DSH reads skills"):

- **How a collection is cut depends on the path** — `~/.agents/skills` and
every other root follow d

ifferent rules:
- **`~/.agents/skills`**: each direct child becomes its own collection,
**named afte

r the child**. The children here are installed skill packs
(one pack, many commands):
- `<name>/SKIL

L.md` — single-skill collection
- `<name>/skills/<s>/SKILL.md` — skill-pack collection, one command

per
skill inside the pack
- `<name>.md` — loose skill collection (name = file stem)
- pure resource

directories (neither layout) are skipped entirely
- **Every other root (e.g. `~/.dsh/skills`)**: the

**whole root is one
collection, named after the root path** (home-relative, shown as
`.dsh/skills`)

. Those roots hold independent single skills; naming a
collection per child would explode into dozen

s of one-command
collections and drown the real grouping. Inside the path collection the
skills are

grouped by **category** instead.
- **Category** has three sources, highest priority first:
1. **Cust

om categories** saved in the panel (see below)
2. the skill frontmatter's `category`
3. **Auto-categ

orization** — keyword extraction from name + description
(weighted, stop-worded), grouped by "same p

rimary topic". Zero config,
zero rule tables.
The category dropdown is **linked to the collection**:

pick a collection
first, then its categories appear.
- **Command** = the skill name (`/name`). Incl

usion rules mirror DSH's source
(`isPotentialSkillPath`, max 2 path segments below the root) plus th

e
skill-pack provider's loading rules.
## Custom categories

Auto-categorization is the zero-config fallback, but if you have **your own
taxonomy** for a skill l

ibrary (e.g. 74 commands split into Onboarding /
Game Design / QA & Testing), paste it once in the p

mands split into Onboarding /
Game Design / QA & Testing), paste it once in the panel and it sticks.
### How to

1. Click **⚙ Categories** at the top right of the panel;
2. pick the **collection** the rules belong

to (defaults to the current
filter; "All collections" matches by command name across collections);
3. paste lines of the form **category name followed by its commands**:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

4. Click **Save & apply**. The panel reports how many categories/commands
were parsed and how many m
atched the current catalog.
[该节后续省略]
### Why refresh / plugin installs & removals never lose it
| Scenario | Mechanism |
| Click ↻ Refresh | Refresh only re-scans `SKILL.md`; every catalog build re-reads and re-applies yo

ur rules |
| Reopen the client / restart DSH | Rules live on disk, independent of any process |
| Un
install/update this plugin | Rules live in `~/.dsh-catalog/`, **not** in the plugin directory and no

t in the `assets/` runtime artifact |
| Another plugin is removed | Rules are stored **by command na
me** and only match, never filter: a missing command keeps its rule and recovers automatically when

the plugin returns |
| Install a new plugin | Commands not in any rule go to `(Uncategorized)` in st
rict mode, otherwise auto-categorization |
## Privacy

- The panel server listens on `127.0.0.1` loopback only, never exposed.
- The scan artifact `assets/

command-catalog.json` contains local absolute
paths; it is a runtime artifact and excluded via `.git

ignore`. The
repository contains no hardcoded local paths or personal data.
- Personalization lives

**outside the repository**: custom categories in
`~/.dsh-catalog/categories.json` (local collection

and command names, not
distributed with the repo).
- Auto-categorization is driven entirely by each

skill's own
name/description; nothing is uploaded and no external service is contacted.
